output.brief: Pellacott's 2026-built VA-220 valves are the problem, and the leak-test certificates behind its improved score appear not to reflect real tests. The independent calibration visit found the only VA-220 test rig out of service since 9 January 2026, with no VA-220 test program on any other rig. Certificate tables repeat four fixed sequences, some already used in November 2025. Brenmoor's lab found 11% of unused 2026 Pellacott valves leak at the seat, against 1% for 2025 builds and 0% for Durrant-Hale. Teardowns show the slide seal deformed. Claim rates are the same across installer and firmware groups, so installers and firmware 4.2 are not the cause. I'm fairly sure of this. Which change is responsible (Corlin seal or Line 3) is not separable yet, and I haven't checked whether other suppliers' records are also unreliable. Next: do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates. Quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and run Brenmoor's own helium testing. Use Durrant-Hale to cover supply. Drop the installer remediation and chargebacks. Require rig logs or witnessed tests in scoring, and audit other suppliers' records.
